newsitem.title: SPAIN: Soros warns British pound is overvalued.
newsitem.headline: Soros warns British pound is overvalued.

text.p: International financier George Soros, the man credited with almost single-handedly driving the British pound out of the Exchange Rate Mechanism in 1992, warned Wednesday that the currency was overvalued against the German mark -- but not against the dollar.

In an interview with Reuters the global fund manager and philanthropist said while he believed the pound was unlikely to join Europe's economic and monetary union at the start in 1999, he was sure Spain, Italy and Portugal would.
He also said he had become more optimistic that the single currency would be launched on time.

On the pound, the sexagenarian billionaire, whose flagship investment fund Quantum is credited with making some $1 billion from the pound's exit from the ERM, said he believed the currency had appreciated too much against the mark.
"I think the pound is overvalued, too strong, against the mark and European currencies," Soros told Reuters after awarding a cultural prize in Madrid.
"However, I don't think the rate against the dollar is worrisome at all," he added.

British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said earlier Wednesday that he shared industry and exporters' concerns about the pound's relentless rise. A survey showed that the currency's strength was denting exporters' confidence as their products become more expensive on world markets.

The pound has appreciated more than 19 percent since last August to five-year peaks at above 2.93 marks in late Europe trade Wednesday. Traders are predicting that the currency will now likely target its old ERM central rate from 1992 at 2.95 marks.
The Hungarian-born financier said the dollar, which has also appreciated sharply in recent months, was not a worry.
"I don't think the dollar has appreciated too fast," he said. However, he added that the higher dollar had benefited European economies.
The dollar has risen to 40-month highs against the mark this week and on Wednesday climbed above 1.75 marks in Europe.
